# Running CRT on your CSR node (operators)

You already run a CKB full node with [CSR](https://github.com/ckb-service-runner/ckb-service-runner) beside it,
registered with a Nervos DAO stake (testnet today; mainnet when CSR's service runtime opens there). CRT is one
more **service** your runner can run. Nothing in your node changes.

## What you commit to

* Your runner keeps one secret per switch it serves — a secp256k1 private key, generated by CSR's CSPRNG inside
  the sandbox and stored in CSR's encrypted service storage, marked secret (never exported or backed up by CSR).
* You publish it on chain when the switch's deadline (+ 24 h) has passed and the owner has not cancelled — the
  service does that in a normal CSR job run; you do nothing.
* You delete it when the owner cancels. CSR does that for you (`delete_on_consume`), even if you disabled the
  service in the meantime.
* You keep the runner online: one heartbeat job run per switch per day (default). Each run pays a tip.

What you cannot do, by construction: release early (consensus refuses the transaction until the deadline) or
release something false (the lock script checks the key against the public key you committed). What you *could*
do and must not: copy a key out of your storage. Users are told that a runner dishonest from day one is outside
the threat model; that is why switches use several runners and thresholds.

## What you earn

Cost table (`SPEC.md` §11; CKB = $0.01, `HEARTBEAT` = 8 000 blocks ≈ 1 day):

| Item | Amount | Spent / locked |
|---|---|---|
| Keygen tip | 1 CKB per runner | spent |
| Heartbeat tip | 0.5 CKB per runner per run → ≈ 183 CKB per runner-year | spent |
| Organiser fee (optional) | default 50 CKB per Create, 0 per Cancel | spent |
| Network fees | < 1 CKB per user transaction | spent |
| Alive Cell | ≈ 61–130 CKB | locked, back on cancel |
| Node Cell | 244 CKB per runner | locked, back on reclaim |
| Keygen job cell | ≈ 288 CKB per runner | locked for hours, back at commit minus tip |
| Heartbeat job cell | ≈ 295 CKB + 365 × 0.502 CKB per runner-year | locked, unspent part back at the end |

The owner pays all of this; you only receive the tips.

| | Default | Per switch-year |
|---|---|---|
| Keygen tip | 1 CKB | 1 CKB |
| Heartbeat tip | 0.5 CKB per daily run | ≈ 183 CKB |

Tips land in your runner wallet like every CSR tip and are swept to your address by CSR. At $0.01 per CKB a
switch pays you about $1.80 a year. **A launch-phase runner is a contribution to the network, not income.** The
owner's own runner is often one of the switch's mandatory nodes; running one for yourself is the first use case.

## Enable

Requires CSR ≥ 0.6.1 (`random_bytes`; check with `csr version`). One script:

```sh
curl -fLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/psawyerberlin/ckb-revocable-timelock/main/scripts/crt-enable.sh
sudo -u csr bash crt-enable.sh --network testnet
```

What it does (see `scripts/crt-enable.sh`; `--dry-run` shows without changing anything):

1. reads your runner lock hash `R` from the running CSR instance;
2. downloads the released `crt-service.elf` and checks its SHA-256 against the release's `SHA256SUMS`;
3. writes a local manifest with `args = R` (this is what makes CRT jobs addressed to *you*, not to any runner —
   `SPEC.md` §3.3) and the CRT deployment data cell;
4. `csr service add-local`, `approve`, `enable`;
5. prints your **CRT service ID** and the dashboard link.

Expected output (abridged; `--dry-run` prints the same steps prefixed `[dry-run]`):

```text
CRT service ID: 0x<64 hex>
Runner lock hash R: 0x<64 hex>
Check the Jobs page of your dashboard (http://127.0.0.1:8114 by default; see csr.toml [dashboard].bind) for CRT jobs.
```

Options: `--network testnet|mainnet` (required), `--dry-run`, `--runner-lock-hash 0x…` (override the value read from
the running CSR). The script refuses to continue if the ELF's SHA-256 differs from the release's `SHA256SUMS`.

Your service ID is derived from public data (`CRT_CODE_HASH`, your `R`, the deployment data hash), so you do not
have to publish anything. To be listed in the client's runner directory, open a pull request adding your runner to
`deployments/<network>-runners.json` (peer id, `R`, a label) — optional; clients can also find you by watching the
chain.

## Watch it

The CSR dashboard's **Jobs** page shows every CRT run with a result `CRT1 <status> <T>`. Per status byte:

| Byte | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `00` hold | deadline + 24 h not reached (or a transient race); no transaction | nothing |
| `01` keygen | fresh key generated, stored, committed (public key in Node Cell) | nothing |
| `02` recommit | key already stored; the commit transaction rebuilt with the same key | nothing |
| `03` release | deadline + 24 h passed, key published | nothing |
| `04` done | Node Cell already released; key deleted | nothing |
| `05` cancelled | owner consumed the Alive Cell; key deleted | nothing |
| `06` dropped | no Node Cell for you on chain; key deleted | nothing |
| `07` **key lost** | committed Node Cell but no usable key in storage, or the key does not match the commitment; no transaction built | storage problem — investigate, tell the owner |
| `08` bad args | service args are not a 32-byte runner lock hash | check the manifest |
| `09` bad payload | job payload or chain answer malformed | ignore, report if repeated |

See `docs/service.md` for the state machine. `service_data/deletions.log` lists the keys CSR deleted on cancellation (never the
content).

## Disable

`scripts/crt-disable.sh` runs `csr service disable` and `revoke`. Switches that chose you lose one node (their
owners see it as headroom shrinking and can rewrap). Keys already stored stay in your storage until the Alive
Cells die — the host rule still applies — unless you delete them by hand (the script prints how). Give users the
time to rewrap: announce before you leave.

## Costs you already carry as a CSR runner

Stake (≥ 10 000 CKB in the Nervos DAO, in your wallet), 700 CKB once for the runner wallet, fees below 1 CKB per
transaction — all documented by CSR. CRT adds no deposit and no slashing.
